You can use the present perfect to refer to past events that are not finished yet. On the other hand, we use the simple past to refer to finished actions in the past.

To create a statement using the present perfect, you need to use the auxiliary verbs HAVE and HAS, and the action verb in its past participle form. Check the following structure:

Subject + auxiliary verb (has/have) + action verb (past participle form) + complement.

Example:
I have designed a well-structured warehouse.
You'd better check the brief descriptions, which I've made, about the features previously mentioned for you to keep them in mind when design time comes.
Finally, you might want to take a look at some design tips: any design method is inoperative if tool support hasn't been done.
Why have the transformation tools been of great relevance for data warehouse implementation?
There were some important features I didn't take into account when I designed a data warehouse.
Remember, always ask yourself: Did I follow the design tips?

To create a negative statement using the present perfect, you need to use the auxiliaries HAVE (I-you-we-they) and HAS (he-she-it) and the particle NOT with an action verb in its past participle form.

The structure we use is:

Subject + auxiliary verb (has/have) + not + action verb (past participle form) + complement.

Example:
We haven't included all of the warehouse features.

To create a question, you need to change the position of the auxiliary verb with the one of the subject. Plus, you need to add a question mark. Now, remember that we make that change when we want to make a yes/no question; plus, take into account that we can add a wh- word at the beginning to make an open question (whose answer is NOT yes or no). Check the structure that we use:

(Wh- question) + Auxiliary verb (has/have) + subject + action verb (past participle form) + complement + ?

Example:
Have you read all of the data warehouse components? (yes/no question)
What have you done to learn about the data warehouse components? (open question)

To create a statement using the simple past, you need to use the verb in its past form; remember there are two types of verbs REGULAR (verbs that you add -ED at the end) and IRREGULAR (verbs that change in spelling and pronunciation).

The structure that we use is the following:

Subject + verb (past form) + complement.

Example:
I used all of the features for the warehouse design. (regular verb)
I began to work on this data warehouse last year. (irregular verb)

To create a negative statement using simple past, you need to use the auxiliary verb did and the negative particle NOT with a verb in its base form.

The structure that we follow is:

Subject + auxiliary verb (did) + not + action verb in base form + complement.

Example:
I did not know what is behind data warehouse design.
I didn't understand what data warehouse was about.

To make a yes /no question, you need to start the question with the auxiliary verb did. On the other hand, if you want to make an open question, you have to use a wh- word plus the auxiliary verb. Check the following structure:

(Wh – word) + did + subject + verb in its base form + complement + ?

Example:
Did you check all of the transformation tools?
Where did you learn about all?
The complete architecture for data warehouse is made up of some important components that need to be included when designing.

A data warehouse is built under seven different main components: database, transformation tools, Meta Data, access tools, Data Marts, information delivery system, and data warehouse administration & management.

Database is the key feature for a warehouse since databases are always used in the management systems. Transformation tools are of great value because by sourcing, acquiring and cleaning up data from operational systems can be put on an appropriate format to be uploaded to the apps that run off the warehouse.

Meta Data refers to data that draws the data warehouse. It is mainly used for building, maintaining and using a data warehouse. It is classified into technical meta data and business meta data. Access tools are all of the possible ways that users have for interacting with the data warehouse.

Data Marts are those different partitions that the warehouse can get. The most relevant information in the Data Marts is obtained from the warehouse. Regarding the information delivery system, we can say that it basically moves the required information to different destinations whenever it is scheduled.
Finally, data warehouse administration & management relates to its security and the management of information.

DATA WAREHOUSE COMPONENTS AND DESIGN YOU MIGHT WANT TO READ ABOUT


There were some important features I didn't take into account when I designed a data warehouse. I needed to include aspects like data collections, tables, table help, data elements, data element help box, and summary data. You'd better check the brief descriptions, which I've made, about the features previously mentioned for you to keep them in mind when design time comes.

Data collections contain information regarding transaction systems. Tables include elements which describe items depending of their importance which helps out when finding facts. Table help gives information about common uses and related tables, and data elements have items that cannot be divided.

<div align="justify">Maybe, you're full of questions about components of data warehouse. Based on my experience, I've created and answered a couple of questions that might be of great importance to you: What are the components of data warehouse? There are seven main components you ought to include when creating data warehouse: database, transformation tools, Meta data, access tools, data Marts, delivery system, and administration & management. Why have the transformation tools been of great relevance for data warehouse implementation? Well, they've been of great value because by sourcing, acquiring and cleaning up data from operational systems, data is organized in an appropriate format to be uploaded to the apps that run off the warehouse. You'd better define what the data dimensions and measures will be in order to succeed with its implementation.</br>

<div align="justify">Finally, you might want to take a look at some design tips: any design method is inoperative if tool support hasn't been done. You ought to perform a conceptual design, bound workload, figure out data magnitude, implement a logical design, and come up with documentation. Remember, always ask yourself: Did I follow the design tips? </br>
